subject: PHB
body: In the CLSI order of draw, which comes first?
explanation: Then light blue, red/gold, green, lavender, gray.

subject: PHB
body: Which tube is drawn immediately after blood cultures?
explanation: Citrate comes early to avoid contamination with other additives.

subject: PHB
body: Which tube is drawn last in the standard order of draw?
explanation: EDTA (lavender) comes just before gray.

subject: PHB
body: A lavender (EDTA) tube is used for
explanation: EDTA preserves cell shape.

subject: PHB
body: A light blue tube must be
options: filled to the correct level to keep the 9:1 blood-to-additive ratio
explanation: Underfilling gives wrong coagulation results.

subject: PHB
body: Tubes with additives should be mixed by
explanation: Shaking can cause haemolysis.

subject: PHB
body: The first-choice vein for venipuncture is usually the
explanation: It is large, well anchored and away from nerves and arteries.

subject: PHB
body: A tourniquet should not be left on for more than
explanation: Longer causes haemoconcentration.

subject: PHB
body: The usual needle insertion angle for venipuncture is
explanation: Bevel facing up.

subject: PHB
body: The site is usually cleaned with
options: 70% isopropyl alcohol and allowed to air dry
explanation: Drawing through wet alcohol can cause haemolysis and stinging.

subject: PHB
body: Before collecting, the patient must be identified using
options: at least two identifiers, such as full name and date of birth
explanation: Ask the patient to state their details.

subject: PHB
body: Specimen tubes should be labeled
options: before the draw at the nurses' station
at the bedside, in front of the patient, after collection
explanation: This prevents mislabeling.

subject: PHB
body: You should avoid drawing blood from the arm
options: on the same side as a mastectomy
explanation: Lymph flow may be impaired.

subject: PHB
body: A hematoma is
options: blood leaking into the tissue around the puncture site
explanation: Apply pressure and don't bend the arm.

subject: PHB
body: If a patient feels faint during a draw, you should
options: remove the tourniquet and needle, and lower the patient's head
explanation: Call for help and monitor them.

subject: PHB
body: Which specimen should be protected from light?
explanation: Light breaks down bilirubin.

subject: PHB
body: Which specimen is commonly transported on ice?
explanation: Chilling slows metabolic changes.

subject: PHB
body: Drug testing specimens require
explanation: It proves the specimen wasn't tampered with.

subject: PHB
body: For an infant heel stick, the puncture should be on
options: the medial or lateral plantar surface of the heel
explanation: Avoid the bone in the center.

subject: PHB
body: Used needles must be
options: activated with the safety device and put straight into a sharps container
explanation: This is required by OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard.

subject: PHB
body: The higher the needle gauge number,
explanation: 21 gauge is standard; 23 gauge butterflies are used for small veins.

subject: PHB
body: The tourniquet is placed about
options: 3 to 4 inches above the puncture site
explanation: Remove it before withdrawing the needle.

subject: PHB
body: If a patient has an IV in one arm, you should
options: draw from the IV line yourself
draw from the other arm if possible
explanation: If you must use that arm, draw below the IV after it has been stopped for at least 2 minutes.

subject: PHB
body: Sites to avoid include
options: scars, burns, swollen (edematous) areas and arms with an AV fistula
explanation: These can affect results or harm the patient.

subject: PHB
body: A serum separator tube (SST) should be inverted about
explanation: EDTA and heparin tubes need 8–10 inversions; citrate 3–4.

subject: PHB
body: In capillary (skin puncture) collection, which is collected first?
explanation: The order differs from venipuncture because platelets clump quickly.

subject: PHB
body: Blood cultures are usually collected
options: as two sets from separate sites, with careful skin antisepsis
explanation: This helps tell true infection from contamination.

subject: PHB
body: A trough drug level is drawn
options: just before the next dose is due
explanation: A peak level is drawn when the concentration is highest.

subject: PHB
body: Tiny red spots on the skin after applying a tourniquet are
explanation: They can indicate a clotting problem; the site may bleed longer.

subject: PHB
body: A specimen label should include
options: the patient's name and ID or date of birth, date, time and collector's initials
explanation: Follow your facility's policy.
